terms.definition: A membrane sac that stores water, salts, nutrients, pigments, and some waste.
terms.function: Provides storage and, in plants, water pressure for support.
terms.whereItIs: In the cytoplasm of both plant and animal cells.
terms.whyItMatters: Storage is how a cell keeps its supplies ready.

terms.definition: The large vacuole in most plant cells that stores water and presses outward.
terms.function: Stores water and creates the firmness (turgor) that keeps plants upright.
terms.whereItIs: Filling most of a typical plant cell.
terms.whyItMatters: It is why a well-watered plant stands tall and a dry one wilts.

terms.definition: The outward push of water inside a plant cell against its wall.
terms.function: Keeps plant cells firm and plants standing upright.
terms.whereItIs: Created by the water-filled vacuole pressing on the cell wall.
terms.whyItMatters: It is the force that gives plants their stiff, leafy shape.
